attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No explicit no-advice generator G_N is known for which H_N has an i.o. N^{1+epsilon} general-circuit lower bound by a non-natural method.
steps: Fix G_N of size N^rho producing m=N^q SAT queries of length L=A(log N)^d and define H_N as their OR.
Assume SAT has circuits of size n^c. Substitute the length-L circuit S_L into every query and add the generator plus OR overhead.
Since L^c=N^{o(1)}, the composed circuit has size N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}, contradicting any i.o. H_N lower bound above N^{1+epsilon} when max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
Audit the independent lookup circuit for SAT_L. It is subthreshold exactly when q+A(log N)^{d-1}<1+epsilon eventually, producing a source-level falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge would separate SAT from P/poly only after the source lower bound is proved. The present work certifies a valid transfer window, not P != NP.

assumptions: G_N is P-uniform or DLOGTIME-uniform, has size N^rho, and outputs N^q well-formed formulas of length L(N).
SAT in P/poly means there is one length-L circuit S_L of size L^c, reused for every generated query at that length.
The OR fan-in N^q and wiring overhead are charged inside SIZE(N^{q+o(1)}).
The lower-bound proof for H_N is not allowed to hardwire the SAT truth table or leak nonuniform query answers.
definitions: source object: H_N^{G,q,L} on x in {0,1}^N, the OR of N^q generated SAT instances of length L(N)=A(log N)^d.
target object: SAT notin P/poly, equivalently NP not subset P/poly for the standard complete language.
controlled interface: compose a single SAT circuit for length L(N) with a uniform generator G_N of size N^rho and an N^q-way OR.
target-preserving condition: max{rho,q}<1+epsilon and no subthreshold lookup/advice circuit computes SAT on the generated length universe.
source lower-bound model: nonuniform Boolean circuits SIZE(s) over N input bits, with an infinitely-often lower bound s>N^{1+epsilon}.
valid length regime: L(N)=A(log_2 N)^d with constants A>0 and d>0; the generator has no satisfiability advice.

dependency_updates.description: Specialized to generated-OR carriers with polylog SAT queries and exact lookup-safety boundary.
Needs i.o. SIZE(N^{1+epsilon}) lower bound for H_N, not a padded SAT lower bound or a natural dense property.
SAT notin P/poly follows only through reusable length-L SAT circuits and no advice leakage.
The obstruction is formal: N^q2^L below N^{1+epsilon} gives an unconditional circuit for H_N.

falsifiers: Lookup falsifier: if d<1, or d=1 with q+A<1+epsilon, the table for SAT_L gives C(H_N)<N^{1+epsilon} and the source premise is impossible.
Threshold falsifier: if rho>=1+epsilon or q>=1+epsilon, SAT-substitution no longer yields a contradiction to the H_N lower bound.
Advice-leakage falsifier: if G_N or the lower-bound proof embeds satisfiability bits for the generated query set, the target-preserving interface to SAT in P/poly is invalid.
Natural-proof falsifier: if the H_N lower bound is obtained via a large constructive property useful against SIZE(N^{1+epsilon}), standard PRF assumptions block it for general circuits.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 15 adds the exact lookup boundary. Polylog queries always preserve all SAT polynomial exponents in the substitution term, but source plausibility requires q+A(log N)^{d-1} not fall below 1+epsilon. Thus d<1 is quarantined, d=1 has a sharp constant window, and d>1 is safely valid from lookup.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate the boundary cases d=1 with A=1+epsilon-q and d=2; search for a generator whose H_N avoids known small-circuit constructions without smuggling SAT advice.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation needs exponentially small soundness epsilon < gamma/2^{O(s log s)} or an equivalent hitting-seed certificate. Standard constant-error AM soundness is insufficient.
steps: Let T={rho: exists w V^{K_N}(rho,w)=1}; completeness gives |T|/2^R >= gamma.
For every size-s circuit C, let B_C={rho: exists w V^{tt(C)}(rho,w)=1}; soundness gives |B_C|/2^R <= epsilon.
The number of such circuits is M(s,m)<=2^{O(s log s)}. Hence |union_C B_C|/2^R <= M(s,m)epsilon.
If gamma > M(s,m)epsilon, choose rho* in T \ union_C B_C.
Define P_{rho*}(f)=1 iff exists w V^f(rho*,w)=1. Then K_N is in P_{rho*}, and no size-s circuit truth table is in P_{rho*}.
Since K_N has an accepting transcript w*, the accepting adaptive path fixes at most q queried bits. All truth tables agreeing with K_N on those bits are accepted, so density is at least 2^{-q}.
If A=O(log N), exhaustive enumeration of w gives a poly(N)-time constructive property; if q=O(log N), the density is polynomially large.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This only audits a route object and may place it inside the natural-proofs barrier. It does not prove P != NP, and it does not rule out non-natural, nonblack-box, or nonuniformly nonconstructive lower-bound methods.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Cycle 15: Public-coin local separators naturalize after global-seed soundness

assumptions: The target circuit class is nonuniform Boolean circuits of size at most s=m^k on m inputs, with truth-table length N=2^m.
The verifier is deterministic once rho,w and oracle answers are fixed; adaptive queries depend only on the previous local transcript.
The random seed rho* may be hardwired into the property description without exceeding the allowed poly(N)-time constructivity budget.
Completeness is for the intended hard truth table K_N, not merely for some promise object unrelated to the target lower bound.
Soundness is universal over all size-s circuits and all existential transcripts w.
definitions: source object: a public-coin local verifier V^{f}(rho,w) for a target truth table K_N, with random seed rho in {0,1}^R, existential transcript w in {0,1}^A, and at most q adaptive queries to f in {0,1}^N.
target object: a Razborov-Rudich style property P_N over N-bit truth tables useful against SIZE(s) circuits, where s=m^k and N=2^m for the audited Boolean-function model.
controlled interface: choose one public seed rho* after a union bound over all size-s circuits, then define P_{rho*}(f)=1 iff there exists w with V^{f}(rho*,w)=1.

target-preserving condition: completeness gives Pr_rho[exists w V^{K_N}(rho,w)=1] >= gamma, soundness gives for every size-s circuit C that Pr_rho[exists w V^{tt(C)}(rho,w)=1] <= epsilon, and gamma exceeds the circuit-count union-bound loss.

equations.label: global_seed_threshold
equations.valid_when: Applies after soundness is measured per fixed circuit but before choosing a single public seed for all circuits.

equations.label: natural_density
equations.valid_when: Requires an accepting transcript for K_N under rho* and at most q deterministic adaptive oracle queries along that accepting path.

equations.label: constructivity_budget
equations.valid_when: Valid when the property algorithm receives the full truth table and enumerates all existential transcripts for the fixed seed.

equations.label: log_threshold
equations.latex: A=O(\log N),\ q=O(\log N) \Rightarrow T_P(N)=\operatorname{poly}(N),\ \mu(P_{\rho^*})\ge N^{-O(1)}
equations.valid_when: Applies when witness length and query complexity are logarithmic in the truth-table length rather than in the original input length.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If soundness is only constant, or if gamma <= M(s,m)epsilon, the union-bound seed may not exist; this is a falsifier to automatic naturalization, not a proof-route escape by itself.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Converts an AM/MA-style local lower-bound certificate into a valid natural property under an explicit quantitative soundness threshold; quarantines public randomness as a claimed escape unless the threshold fails.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A public-coin local truth-table separator with logarithmic query and witness lengths is still a natural-proof object if its soundness is small enough to union-bound over all target small circuits. Randomness is not a barrier escape unless the route refuses the global-seed certificate or loses constructivity.

assumptions: There are M(s,m) possible target circuits.
The verifier's public randomness is visible to the property designer.
No additional pseudorandom or hitting-set structure on bad seed sets is assumed.
definitions: Let B_C={rho: exists w V^{tt(C)}(rho,w)=1}. Constant soundness only gives |B_C|/2^R <= 1/3 for each C.
Usefulness of a fixed-seed property requires one rho outside union_C B_C.
The obstruction is quantitative, not relativization or algebrization.

equations.label: union_bound_failure
equations.valid_when: Valid when only per-circuit constant soundness is available and no correlation information between bad seed sets is known.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A route that cites AM-style locality but supplies no exponentially small soundness remains unaudited and cannot be classified as a valid natural-proof object.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents overclaiming from randomized local certificates; it identifies the exact missing amplification or structure.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Constant-error public-coin local soundness does not by itself naturalize, because every small circuit may have a disjoint accepting seed set and their union can cover all public coins.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the route cannot supply exponentially small soundness, a hitting-set replacement, or a uniform way to choose rho* without losing the target-preserving condition.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote further if amplification preserves q=O(log N), A=O(log N), and excludes all SIZE(m^k) circuits with epsilon below 2^{-O(m^k log m)}.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a named bridge lemma with source model, target class, and quantitative threshold. It also identified the exact blocking gap for AM-style constant soundness.

dependency_updates.description: Public-coin local certificates naturalize only after global-seed soundness epsilon < gamma/2^{O(s log s)}; constant soundness is a quantitative gap.
The seed-fixing argument is black-box in the truth table and would relativize unless the underlying verifier uses nonrelativizing syntax elsewhere.
No algebraic extension mechanism is used; the present obstruction is naturalness and explicitness, not algebrization.
Hardwiring rho* is harmless only if the property model permits that nonuniform seed or if rho* is found uniformly in poly(N) time.

falsifiers: falsifier: constant per-circuit soundness lets bad seed sets for exponentially many small circuits cover every public seed, so no useful fixed-seed property follows.
falsifier: A=omega(log N) can destroy poly(N) constructivity even if a good seed exists.
falsifier: q=omega(log N) can make the accepting cylinder exponentially small, outside the standard largeness threshold.
falsifier: if rho* requires superpolynomial advice to find and cannot be hardwired within the accepted property model, the transfer loses explicitness.
falsifier: if soundness quantifies only against honest provers rather than all transcripts for small circuits, P_{rho*} may accept easy truth tables.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: There is a threshold near alpha larger than the circuit-count constant. Above it, a global seed exists and the protocol yields a valid natural property of density N^{-O(1)}. Below it, constant or weak soundness gives no useful seed and public randomness is not yet barrier-classified.
held_fixed_controls: Target class remains nonuniform SIZE(m^k) on m inputs.
Query bound is q=c log N and witness length is A=c' log N.
Completeness gamma is fixed at 2/3 for the SAT_m truth table.

gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch has already naturalized deterministic, advised, randomized-local, and short-Merlin certificates. The remaining plausible escape is public randomness; a concrete seed-fixing experiment decides whether randomness changes the barrier status or only adds a union-bound threshold.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Consider an AM-local separator for the SAT_m truth table of length N=2^m. The verifier uses public seed rho, an existential transcript w, and q adaptive truth-table queries. It claims to reject every SIZE(m^k) truth table with small error.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal amplification or hitting-seed lemma proving gamma > M(s,m)epsilon while preserving q=O(log N), A=O(log N), target class SIZE(m^k), and poly(N) constructivity.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The varied parameter is the soundness exponent alpha in epsilon=2^{-alpha m^k log m}.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 15 isolates the public-randomness threshold for local separator routes. Random coins are not automatically a natural-proof escape: if soundness is exponentially small enough to beat the 2^{O(s log s)} circuit count, one seed makes an existential local property useful, large, and poly(N)-constructive. Constant soundness is the precise falsifier to this transfer. This is valid route-level barrier progress, not evidence for P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit whether parallel repetition or error reduction for public-coin local truth-table separators can reduce epsilon below 2^{-O(s log s)} without increasing q or A beyond O(log N); if not, quarantine AM-local certificates as constant-error non-naturalized objects rather than barrier escapes.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No construction is known for a sparse sound source whose verifier state is provably impossible to restart below exponent epsilon without already proving a circuit lower bound.
steps: Fix accepted c_m and block size B=2^{alpha m}; on input x in {0,1}^m compute index i, boundary j=floor(i/B), and offset r.
Use R_m(c_m,j) to obtain the verifier state at time jB with circuit size 2^{sigma m+o(m)}; hardwiring c_m costs only O(m).
Unroll the deterministic streaming update for r<B steps and output bit i, giving size 2^{max(alpha,sigma)m+o(m)}.
If max(alpha,sigma)<epsilon-o(1), this contradicts MCSP no-side soundness C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m}; hence valid sources must defeat all such restarts.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-level obstruction and quantitative source obligation only; it neither constructs the carrier nor proves P != NP.

assumptions: For infinitely or kappa-densely many m, V_m accepts c_m and emits T_m with |T_m|=2^m.
A restart map R_m(c,j) returns the exact verifier state at boundary jB, where B=2^{alpha m}.
R_m has uniform circuits or time 2^{sigma m+o(m)} after hardwiring the O(m)-bit certificate.
The accepted-source property is sparse/non-large; a dense constructive version triggers the natural-proofs falsifier.
definitions: source object: sequential certificates c_m of length O(m) for a verifier V_m that streams a truth table T_m in time 2^{O(m)} and is sound for C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m}.
target object: an E language L_T obtained by uniform search over kappa-dense source lengths, aiming for L_T notin SIZE(2^{delta n}) for every delta<epsilon/kappa.
controlled interface: MCSP no-side soundness at threshold N^epsilon with N=2^m, plus E-time extraction that only reads sequential streams and never receives nonuniform selectors.
target-preserving condition: any restart, checkpoint, address, or selector mechanism must be uniform and counted in the bit-circuit size; subepsilon leakage is an invalid transfer.

falsifier: brute-force enumeration of circuits only certifies s=O(m/log m), so epsilon_m=O(log m/m) and the transfer collapses to delta=o(1).
falsifier: a dense constructive recognizer for acceptable streams is a natural-proofs obstruction; the route must stay sparse/non-large and nonuniform-free.
